content:
Check the bottle before you take another capsule. A single lot of 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha Capsules, in 120-count bottles, has been recalled over possible salmonella contamination, according to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

The recalled product was made by Vitality Works Inc. of Albuquerque, New Mexico, and was sold at Whole Foods Market stores nationwide and online at Amazon between November 24, 2025 and October 20, 2026. The potential contamination was identified through routine sampling of a single retail unit, the FDA said.

How to tell if your bottle is affected

  • Product: 365 Whole Foods Market Standardized + Full Spectrum Blend Ashwagandha Capsules, 120 count, in a white plastic bottle
  • Lot number: 2025-26227
  • UPC: 9948252099
  • Expiration date: October 13, 2028

Only that one lot is covered by the recall. No illnesses connected to the recall had been reported as of the FDA announcement.

Consumers are advised to stop using the product, discard it, and not return it to the place of purchase — though a refund is available at any Whole Foods Market. Vitality Works Inc. can be reached at 505-268-9950. Salmonella is a foodborne illness that, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, can cause stomach cramps, diarrhea and vomiting.

Sources:

  • USA TODAY — Whole Foods supplement recalled over salmonella risk
  • Louisiana First News — Supplements sold at Whole Foods recalled

title: Check the Bottle: Whole Foods Ashwagandha Capsules Recalled Over Possible Salmonella
